bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.topic: Dow Theory & Primary Averages -> Classical Chart Patterns & Trendline Breakouts
facts.statement: Limitation of Dow Theory & Primary Averages: Dow Theory confirms only after 20% to 30% of a primary trend has already unfolded, missing early reversal turns and exposing late entrants to severe drawdowns.. Solution: Classical Chart Patterns & Trendline Breakouts via Head and Shoulders necklines, double bottoms, and trendlines pinpoint exact entry pivots at the earliest inflection points..

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.topic: Classical Chart Patterns -> Moving Averages & Momentum Oscillators (RSI, MACD, Stochastics)
facts.statement: Limitation of Classical Chart Patterns: Drawing lines on charts is subjective; in sideways horizontal trading ranges, chartists suffer repeated whipsaws and expensive false breakouts.. Solution: Moving Averages & Momentum Oscillators (RSI, MACD, Stochastics) via Mathematical price smoothing eliminates subjective line-drawing bias, while oscillators quantify overbought and oversold extremes..

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.topic: Single-Indicator Trading Systems -> Japanese Candlesticks & Volume Confirmation
facts.statement: Limitation of Single-Indicator Trading Systems: Moving averages whipsaw endlessly in non-trending ranges, while oscillators get pinned at overbought levels during runaway trends, giving false sell signals.. Solution: Japanese Candlesticks & Volume Confirmation via Candlestick price action (Hammers, Engulfing, Dojis) provides immediate 1-to-3 bar confirmation, while volume confirms true institutional accumulation..

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.topic: Isolated Technical Chart Setups -> Intermarket Analysis & Market Breadth
facts.statement: Limitation of Isolated Technical Chart Setups: Textbook technical breakouts on individual stocks collapse instantly if the broader sector is distributing or bond yields and commodity inflation trigger systemic risk.. Solution: Intermarket Analysis & Market Breadth via Cross-asset correlation across currencies, commodities, bonds, and equities, combined with advance-decline breadth to anticipate market turns weeks in advance..

facts.statement: Market action discounts all fundamental news, earnings reports, rumors, and crowd psychology into price. Directive: Never argue with prevailing price action; if good earnings news causes a stock to plunge, respect the distribution signal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Prices move in trends, and higher-timeframe primary trends always overrule minor intraday ripples. Directive: Always identify the weekly primary trend first; execute tactical long entries only when the weekly trend is bullish.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Trading volume must definitively expand in the direction of the primary trend to validate price moves. Directive: Demand above-average volume on breakouts; treat low-volume breakouts as high-risk institutional liquidity traps.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Broken support levels become future resistance ceilings, and broken resistance levels become future support floors. Directive: Look to buy former resistance ceilings on initial pullbacks with tight stops placed just beneath the broken level.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Different technical tools possess distinct operational domains: moving averages excel in trends, while oscillators excel in ranges. Directive: Check ADX trend strength: if ADX is above 25 use moving averages; if ADX is below 20 trade oscillator overbought/oversold extremes.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Indicators and chart patterns establish prospective zones, but Japanese candlesticks provide the immediate execution trigger. Directive: Wait for a Hammer, Bullish Engulfing, or Piercing pattern at key support before pulling the trigger on an entry.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: Technical analysis without strict risk control is financial suicide; capital preservation is the first duty of the chartist. Directive: Never risk more than 1% to 2% of total account capital per trade, and demand prospective gains that are at least 3x the stop distance.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets (John J. Murphy)

facts.statement: No individual asset class trades in isolation; bond yields, commodity inflation, and currencies dictate equity market trends. Directive: Monitor 10-year Treasury yields and advance-decline breadth weekly; reduce equity exposure when yields surge and breadth diverges.
